s1.syndrome_frame: cutaneous vascular lesion with telangiectasias in a patient with metastatic cancer
salient_findings: single, well-defined, blanchable bright red plaque on the lower right lateral shin
discrete clusters of small-caliber vessels on histopathological analysis
KDR (VEGFR2) c.C2312G, p.T771R somatic mutation identified
key_facts: patient is a man in his 40s
patient has stage IV KRAS wild-type rectal adenocarcinoma
patient has pulmonary and liver metastases
patient has undergone radiation therapy and multiple chemotherapy cycles
lesion developed in early January 2015
lesion is 4 cm in diameter
lesion is not associated with pain or pruritus
histopathological analysis shows normal epidermis
genetic analysis was performed using paired whole-exome sequencing

shortlist.label: cutaneous metastasis
shortlist.why_kept: patient has metastatic cancer and developed a cutaneous lesion

shortlist.label: telangiectasia
shortlist.why_kept: histopathological analysis shows discrete clusters of small-caliber vessels

shortlist.label: angiosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: patient has a history of radiation therapy and developed a vascular lesion

shortlist.label: bacillary angiomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: patient is immunocompromised due to cancer and chemotherapy

shortlist.label: pyogenic granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: lesion is a well-defined, blanchable red plaque with telangiectasias

raw.rationale: The lesion is described as a blanchable bright red plaque densely composed of telangiectasias, and histopathological analysis shows discrete clusters of small-caliber vessels, consistent with telangiectasia.

rejected.label: cutaneous metastasis
rejected.why: The histopathological analysis does not show evidence of metastatic cancer cells in the lesion.

rejected.label: angiosarcoma
rejected.why: The histopathological analysis does not show evidence of malignant vascular tumor cells, and the lesion is described as benign-appearing.

rejected.label: bacillary angiomatosis
rejected.why: There is no mention of Bartonella infection or other typical features of bacillary angiomatosis.

rejected.label: pyogenic granuloma
rejected.why: The lesion is not described as having the typical features of pyogenic granuloma, such as rapid growth or ulceration.
